correctness.rationale: An independent all-k argument checks the nonequivariant input: for a path on m≥3 vertices, splitting at the next-to-last vertex gives a conical deletion and a link on m−3 vertices, shifting reduced homology by one. Splitting the 3k-cycle at 0 gives deletion P_(3k−1) and link P_(3k−3), with their unique reduced groups Z in degrees k−1 and k−2 for k≥2. The integral exact sequence gives a split extension of Z by Z in degree k−1 and no other groups. At k=1 the complex has three vertices. For all k each join chain z_j is closed by signed omission cancellation, and its support lies in independent sets. The two maximal independent residue-class faces give actual integral cocycles even in the presence of higher simplices. Their evaluation on z_0,z_1 has rows (1,0), ((−1)^k,1) and determinant 1, proving a full basis. On z_2 it is (−1,0), the −1 coming from k negative choices and a cyclic factor reorder of sign (−1)^(k−1). Hence [z_2]=−a+(−1)^k b. Rotation shifts the offsets, and reflection sends factor t of z_j to reversed pair k−1−t of z_(2−j); reversing the k factors and the k directed pairs gives (−1)^(k(k+1)/2). These give exactly the stated column action matrices. With r=1 the relations give a=b and (2−(−1)^k)a=0; for odd k, s acts on the remaining Z/3 by (−1)^(k(k+1)/2). This proves both module-coinvariant assertions, including the triangle boundary case. No finite testing is used to infer the infinite result.
residual_risks: This is an action on reduced homology, not the topology or homology of the geometric orbit complex. Signs depend on the specified orientations and the distinguished reflection.

evidence: Adamaszek/Kozlov gives nonequivariant homotopy information. The triple-saturation result treats Ind(C_(3m)^(m−1)) as an integral order-three rotation module, not an ordinary cycle dihedral module.

At m=2 there is an actual match of the restriction to g=r² in Ind(C_6): R²=[[-1,−1],[1,0]] is conjugate over Z to [[0,−1],[1,−1]] by P=[[1,−1],[0,1]] in the relation P^(-1)R²P. That case does not determine the reflection, the full D_6 module, or the family.

evidence: For odd k the rational rotation realizes multiplication by ζ3. Multiplication by ζ3−ζ3² commutes with rotation and conjugates S to −S, so the two reflections yield the same rational dihedral character. Their integral full-dihedral coinvariants nevertheless differ: the cyclic quotient is Z/3 and exactly one of the opposite reflection signs preserves it.
The prior rank-two ordinary homology result has no reflection choice, and the power-of-cycle comparison supplies only the indicated rotation restriction.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact orientation action on an integral basis is additional information: even a complete rational character cannot distinguish the exhibited integral possibilities, and none of the other compared results supplies that missing distinction.

evidence: The matching complex of a cycle identifies with the independence complex of its line graph, again a cycle; cc3173e88c15 computes geometric quotients for 3≤n≤13. For n=9 that quotient is contractible, while the claimed module coinvariants are Z/3.

The theta/noncover complex is Alexander dual to the given independence complex. In this free case its homology lattice is the dual of the original homology in complementary degree n−(k−1)−3=2k−2, twisted by the sign of the ambient vertex permutation. e761de5afaa9 computes the rational character only and excludes an integral determination when 3 divides n.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An integral classification of the dual lattice with the proper sign twist would be equivalent coverage. A rational character or the geometric orbit-space homology is not that classification.

value.rationale: A canonical all-k family gets concrete geometric generators and the full lattice action, not merely an isomorphism after scalar extension. The precise mod-four criterion detects order-three module coinvariants that the rational character cannot distinguish, and supplies useful input for computations with the symmetries of the ordinary cycle matching complex. The sign and integral basis matter: a rational basis or a finite catalogue of examples would not give the result.
residual_risks: No claim about geometric quotients, all cycle powers, or a determination of other equivariant topological invariants.
